question: How do you use Flask-SQLAlchemy for database access in Flask?
title: Flask-SQLAlchemy Integration
direct_answer: Flask-SQLAlchemy wraps SQLAlchemy with Flask-aware session management. Models inherit from db.Model. db.session is the request-scoped session (automatically committed or rolled back via teardown). @db.event.listens_for for model hooks. db.create_all() in the app context to create tables. The session is tied to the request context — never use it outside a request or app context.

sections.title: Flask-SQLAlchemy setup
sections.content:
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from datetime import datetime

db = SQLAlchemy()

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(db.String(255), unique=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=datetime.utcnow)

# In create_app()
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'postgresql://...'
db.init_app(app)

# CRUD in views
@users_bp.route('/', methods=['POST'])
def create_user():
    user = User(email=request.json['email'])
    db.session.add(user)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'id': user.id}), 201

# Query
user = User.query.filter_by(email='test@example.com').first()
# SQLAlchemy 2.0 style
result = db.session.execute(select(User).where(User.email == 'test@example.com'))

seo.metaTitle: Flask-SQLAlchemy — Models, Session Management, and Queries
seo.metaDescription: Flask-SQLAlchemy: db.Model for models, request-scoped db.session, CRUD operations, and migration with Flask-Migrate.

speakable_v2.hook: Flask-SQLAlchemy ties SQLAlchemy's session to Flask's request context — it handles setup and teardown so you don't have to.

beats.content: db.session is request-scoped. Flask-SQLAlchemy commits on successful response and rolls back on error. Add objects with db.session.add(), remove with db.session.delete().
Models inherit from db.Model. Use Mapped[] annotations for SQLAlchemy 2.0 compatibility. db.init_app(app) in the factory wires up the session to the app context.

speakable_v2.cap: Set SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS = False in config — the default (None) shows a deprecation warning and uses extra memory.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Flask-Migrate for Alembic integration, or query patterns in SQLAlchemy 2.0.
